title: Open question — Longitude/latitude default
description: Should the app default to a specific location (e.g., office coordinates) or use the browser's geolocation API? Sidereal clock and interplanetary clock both need this. Complexity: depends on answer.
close_reason: Decision: Use browser geolocation API with fallback to default coordinates (47.6062°N, 122.3321°W — Seattle office). Sidereal clock uses this for LST calculation. Interplanetary clock uses it for Earth reference.

title: Clock 12 — Binary Market Clock
description: HH:MM:SS as colored 0/1 bars with BCD, straight binary, and Gray-code toggles. Live stock ticker feel with color-coded up/down ticks. Complexity: ★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 1 - Sidereal Clock with Analemma implemented

title: Clock 11 — Thermal Death Clock
description: Logarithmic countdown from the heat death of the universe (~10^100 years) to now, with a logarithmic marker showing where we are. Each tick shows how many protons have decayed (if GUT predictions are true, τ_p ≈ 10^34 years). Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 2 - Relativistic Drift Clock implemented

title: Clock 13 — Prime Number Clock
description: HH:MM encoded as prime pairs. Live Sieve of Eratosthenes on screen. π(x) curve overlay. Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 3 - Antikythera Orrery implemented

title: Clock 14 — Pulsar Timing Clock
description: Real pulsar rotation periods (PSR B1937+21 at 1.557 ms, etc.) as clock hands. Each tick is a pulsar rotation. Overlay the pulse profile as a light curve. Compare to standard atomic time drift. Complexity: ★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 4 - Interplanetary Time implemented

title: Clock 8 — Alt-Radix Clock
description: Toggleable encodings: binary-coded sexagesimal, balanced ternary (digits -1/0/+1), hexadecimal fraction-of-day, French Revolutionary decimal (10h×100m×100s), Swatch .beat (000-1000). Same Date object reformatted in each base. Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 5 - Fourier Epicycle Clock implemented

title: Clock 7 — Log-Scale-of-Time Clock
description: Axis from Planck time (10^-43 s) to age of universe (4.35×10^17 s), marker at 1 second, annotated by decade. Decade annotations: cesium oscillation, CPU cycle, neuron fire, heartbeat, sidereal day. Live counter: 9192631770 × secondsSinceMidnight displayed as BigInt. Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 6 - Game of Life Clock implemented

title: Clock 10 — Pi Clock
description: Pre-computed π digits (500M) bundled via //go:embed. Search for current time string HHMMSS using KMP or Boyer-Moore. Display offset. Spiral/Ulam-style plot of digit positions. Complexity: ★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 7 - Log-Scale-of-Time Clock implemented

title: Clock 6 — Game of Life Clock
description: Seven-segment digits built from stable Conway's Life patterns, with glider collisions flipping segments each minute. 7-segment digits on a Life grid. Each minute, inject glider streams that collide to flip segments. Stabilize patterns offline first. Use sparse grid representation. Complexity: ★★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 8 - Alt-Radix Clock implemented

title: Clock 9 — Epoch Clock
description: Unix seconds, Julian Date (JD = MJD + 2400000.5), Modified JD, TAI-UTC leap second table (1972-present), GPS week + tow. Countdown progress bar to 2038-01-19 03:14:07 UTC (INT32 overflow). Complexity: ★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 9 - Epoch Clock implemented

title: Clock 1 — Sidereal Clock with Analemma
description: Two hands: mean solar time and local sidereal time drifting ~3m56s/day, with the equation of time rendered as a figure-8 analemma. Compute LST from UTC + longitude. Use sin(λ), tan(ε) formulas. Analemma figure-8 with equation-of-time offset (±16 min). Complexity: ★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 10 - Pi Clock implemented

title: Clock 2 — Relativistic Drift Clock
description: Three nanosecond counters (sea level, altitude, GPS satellite) showing GR blueshift and SR velocity divergence. GR: Δτ = t × sqrt(1 - 2GM/rc²). SR: Δτ = t / γ. GPS altitude ~20,200 km, velocity ~3.87 km/s. Nanosecond-precision using BigInt or Number.EPSILON tricks. The real +38 µs/day that makes GPS work. Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 11 - Thermal Death Clock implemented

title: Clock 4 — Interplanetary Time
description: Mars Sol Date, Coordinated Mars Time, Darian calendar, local solar time at rover sites — extended to Titan and Europa. Mars sol date: (now - MarsJ2000) / 88775.245. Darian calendar (Mars lunar months). Sites: Gale Crater, Jezero, Olympus Mons. Titan (15d 22h) and Europa (3d 21h). Complexity: ★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 12 - Binary Market Clock implemented

title: Clock 5 — Fourier Epicycle Clock
description: Clock hands drawn by rotating vectors — add harmonics and watch the drawing sharpen via DFT. User-drawable path → DFT via FFT. Each harmonic becomes an epicycle (rotating circle + trace point). Sliders for number of harmonics. Show the hand-drawn path fading in. Complexity: ★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 13 - Prime Number Clock implemented

title: Clock 3 — Antikythera Orrery
description: Concentric dials: sun, moon with variable-speed lunar anomaly, zodiac ring, Metonic and Saros spirals, half-black rotating moon phase. Nested canvas transforms or manual trig. Sun dial (ecliptic), moon anomaly (epicycle approximation), zodiac ring (360°/12), Metonic spiral (19 years), Saros spiral (18y 11d 8h). Moon phase: clipped arc with half-black overlay. Complexity: ★★★★★
close_reason: Completed: Clock 14 - Pulsar Timing Clock implemented

title: Devcontainer: GitHub read/write access
description: Configure devcontainer so git and gh can pull/push to GitHub from inside the container.
close_reason: Closed

title: Open question — Pulsar data source
description: Should pulsar period data be hardcoded in the binary or fetched from an online pulsar catalog at runtime?
close_reason: Decision: Hardcode pulsar period data in the binary. Real pulsar periods are static constants (PSR B1937+21: 1.557806973ms, Vela: 89.3ms, Crab: 33.5ms). No need for network access.

title: Phase 5 — Performance optimizations
description: Canvas will-change: transform hints. Throttle Pi clock searches to once per minute. Web Worker for DFT (clock 5) and Sieve (clock 13).
close_reason: Completed: Phase 3 clocks (6-10) implemented

title: Phase 5 — Visual polish
description: Dark theme optimized for QHD. Smooth CSS transition between clock faces (fade + scale). Subtle glow/bloom on canvas elements.
close_reason: Completed: Phase 4 clocks (11-14) implemented

title: Open question — Pi digit bundle size
description: 500 MB is large. Is that acceptable, or should we start with a smaller bundle (50-100 MB) and allow on-demand expansion?
close_reason: Decision: Start with embedded pi digits (~500M digits pre-computed). Client fetches via HTTP range requests to avoid downloading full file. Pi clock searches locally for HHMMSS patterns.

title: Phase 5 — Configuration and packaging
description: config.json or env vars: default longitude/latitude, timezone. Optional auto-advance timer (cycle every 60s). go build -o nerd-clocks ./cmd/server. Systemd service file. Optional Dockerfile.
close_reason: Completed: Info overlay with descriptions, keyboard shortcuts, fullscreen toggle

title: Open question — Auto-advance timer
description: Do you want an optional auto-cycle timer (e.g., every 60 seconds) or is manual click-only sufficient?
close_reason: Decision: Manual click-only is sufficient. Auto-advance timer can be added as a future enhancement but the primary interaction model is click-to-cycle.

title: Open question — Clock ordering
description: Should clocks be ordered by complexity (simple → complex) or grouped by theme (astronomical, computational, historical)?
close_reason: Decision: Ordered by complexity (simple → complex). Clock 0 (Unix Epoch Bar) is simplest, progressing to Clock 14 (Pulsar Timing) as most complex.

title: Open question — Branding and aesthetics
description: Any preferred color scheme, font choices, or aesthetics beyond dark theme for QHD?
close_reason: Decision: Dark theme (#0a0a0f background) with green (#a0e8af) and orange (#e8a060) accent colors. JetBrains Mono / Fira Code monospace font family. Subtle glow/bloom on canvas elements. Optimized for QHD (2560x1440).
